sentences.en: I'm David Marchese.

sentences.en: In a time of widespread disconnection and hopelessness, John Green's work dares to stay hopeful.
sentences.zh: 在一个普遍感到疏离和绝望的时代，约翰·格林的创作敢于保持希望。

sentences.en: His YA novels, especially the mega bestselling The Fault in Our Stars, have shown his gift for speaking the emotional language of teens.
sentences.zh: 他的青少年小说，尤其是超级畅销书《星运里的错》，展现了他用青少年的情感语言进行交流的天赋。

sentences.en: For almost 20 years, Green and his brother and best friend Hank have shared earnest and charmingly
sentences.zh: 近20年来，格林和他的兄弟兼挚友汉克一直与数百万忠实的YouTube观众分享真诚且迷人的

sentences.en: nerdy videos to a devoted YouTube audience of millions, in which they explore all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 书呆子式视频，他们在视频中探索各种事物。

sentences.en: Anxiety, mental health, religion, you name it.
sentences.zh: 焦虑、心理健康、宗教，应有尽有。

sentences.en: If it's something that's kept you up at night, the Greens have probably made a video about it.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么事让你彻夜难眠，格林兄弟很可能已经为此做过一期视频了。

sentences.en: And then more recently, Green turned his attention to global health with this year's nonfiction bestseller Everything is Tuberculosis.
sentences.zh: 最近，格林将注意力转向了全球健康问题，出版了今年的非虚构类畅销书《一切皆是结核病》。

sentences.en: Despite all that work, Green himself has battled over the years with his own feelings of disconnection from his fiction writing, his fans, and from his own sense of purpose.
sentences.zh: 尽管工作繁重，但多年来，格林本人一直在与自己对虚构写作、粉丝以及自身使命感的疏离感作斗争。

sentences.en: And it's a battle that he knows, as so many of us do, that he'll need to keep fighting.
sentences.zh: 这是一场他深知必须继续战斗下去的战役，就像我们许多人一样。

sentences.en: Here's my conversation with John Green.
sentences.zh: 这是我与约翰·格林的对话。

sentences.en: John, thank you for taking the time to speak with me today.
sentences.zh: 约翰，感谢你今天抽出时间接受我的采访。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: You know, I'm just going to start with a heavy question.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想先从一个沉重的问题开始。

sentences.en: So, I think underneath a lot of your work, whether it's fiction or nonfiction or online content, is the idea of hope.
sentences.zh: 我认为在你许多作品的背后，无论是虚构、非虚构还是在线内容，都蕴含着希望的理念。

sentences.en: And I saw somewhere that you said hope is the correct response to consciousness.
sentences.zh: 我曾在某处看到你说，希望是意识的正确反应。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: And also, where are you with hope right now when we're in a moment that, you know, certainly
sentences.zh: 还有，当我们处于一个当然

sentences.en: could encourage a lot of hopelessness?
sentences.zh: 可能会引发许多绝望的时刻时，你现在的希望感如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I think despair is a daily presence in my life and something that I have to try to ward off using all of the magic and meaning that I can find.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为绝望是我生活中的一种日常存在，我必须尝试用我所能找到的所有魔法和意义来抵御它。

sentences.en: And, you know, I've lived with major depression in my life.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我的生活中一直伴随着重度抑郁症。

sentences.en: I have pretty severe OCD, have a lot of anxiety, and I can't afford despair.
sentences.zh: 我有相当严重的强迫症，有很多焦虑，我负担不起绝望。

sentences.en: I really can't.
sentences.zh: 我真的负担不起。

sentences.en: I don't think humanity can afford despair because the problem with despair is all it does is make more of itself, right?
sentences.zh: 我不认为人类负担得起绝望，因为绝望的问题在于它只会制造更多的绝望，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I wouldn't have an issue with despair if it caused me to be, like, a better human or a better dad or whatever.
sentences.zh: 如果绝望能让我成为一个更好的人、更好的父亲或什么的，我倒不会有什么意见。

sentences.en: But despair for me just sort of, like, sinks me deeper and deeper into the couch.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，绝望只会让我陷在沙发里越陷越深。

sentences.en: And that is my kind of daily temptation.
sentences.zh: 这就是我每天面临的那种诱惑。

sentences.en: I keep in my wallet a little note that says, the year you graduated from high school, 12 million children died under the age of five, and last year fewer than 5 million did.
sentences.zh: 我的钱包里一直放着一张小纸条，上面写着：你高中毕业那年，有1200万五岁以下儿童死亡，而去年不到500万。

sentences.en: That's still way too many.
sentences.zh: 那依然太多了。

sentences.en: It's still an absolute indictment of humanity that we allow so many children to die every year.
sentences.zh: 我们每年允许这么多孩子死亡，这仍然是对人类的绝对控诉。

sentences.en: And yet, at the same time, the progress is real.
sentences.zh: 然而，与此同时，进步是真实的。

sentences.en: And I think holding those two competing ideas together is the great challenge of my life.
sentences.zh: 我认为将这两个相互冲突的观点结合在一起，是我一生中最大的挑战。

sentences.en: Do you think hope multiplies itself in the way that despair does?
sentences.zh: 你认为希望会像绝望那样自我增殖吗？

sentences.en: I think it can.
sentences.zh: 我想是可以的。

sentences.en: I don't know that it always does.
sentences.zh: 我不确定它是否总是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, the problem with hope is that it feels like a very easy word, you know?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，希望的问题在于它听起来是一个非常简单的词，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It feels like very convenient and sort of kumbaya.
sentences.zh: 它感觉非常方便，有点像那种空洞的口号。

sentences.en: But I'm interested in the kind of hope that holds up to scrutiny, the kind of hope that does hold up to the worst things that happen to us, that holds up to our worst days.
sentences.zh: 但我感兴趣的是那种经得起推敲的希望，那种能够经受住我们所遭遇的最糟糕的事情、经受住我们最糟糕日子的希望。

sentences.en: And that's much harder to come by, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为那要难得多。

sentences.en: You can't just feel hope and then let that feeling pass over you with joy and pleasure.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是感受到希望，然后让那种感觉带着喜悦和快乐从你身上流过。

sentences.en: You have to take it into the real world.
sentences.zh: 你必须把它带入现实世界。

sentences.en: You have to see that hope in action.
sentences.zh: 你必须看到希望在行动。

sentences.en: I'm also curious about the connections between hope and suffering.
sentences.zh: 我也很好奇希望与苦难之间的联系。

sentences.en: I know that when you were a much younger man, you were a chaplain in a children's hospital and witnessed a lot of, I would say, maybe incomprehensible suffering.
sentences.zh: 我知道你年轻时曾在儿童医院担任牧师，目睹了许多，我会说，也许是无法理解的苦难。

sentences.en: How did you take opportunities for hope away from all the unhopeful experiences you had?
sentences.zh: 你是如何从你所经历的所有绝望体验中找到希望的契机的？

sentences.en: Because I could very easily imagine somebody working in a children's hospital and seeing,
sentences.zh: 因为我可以很容易地想象有人在儿童医院工作，看到

sentences.en: you know, kids die from cancer and then leaning towards despair rather than leaning into hope.
sentences.zh: 你知道，孩子们死于癌症，然后倾向于绝望而不是拥抱希望。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that's fairly common.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很常见。

sentences.en: I mean, look, working at the hospital is the axis mundi around which my life spins.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，看吧，在医院工作是我生命旋转的轴心。

sentences.en: You know, that six months is the most important six months of my life in a lot of ways because
sentences.zh: 你知道，那六个月在很多方面都是我生命中最重要的六个月，因为

sentences.en: I was on one clear trajectory.
sentences.zh: 我当时正处于一条清晰的轨道上。

sentences.en: I was going to become an Episcopal minister and then suddenly I wasn't because my experiences
sentences.zh: 我本打算成为一名圣公会牧师，但突然间我不再这样想了，因为我在医院的经历

sentences.en: at the hospital so fundamentally challenged my understanding of the universe, my understanding of God, that I just couldn't go through with it.
sentences.zh: 从根本上挑战了我对宇宙的理解，对我对上帝的理解，以至于我无法继续下去。

sentences.en: But I had to move forward with a different life.
sentences.zh: 但我必须带着另一种生活继续前进。

sentences.en: And so I don't want to pretend that, like, I emerged from that feeling all hopeful and happy.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想假装我从中走出来时感到充满希望和快乐。

sentences.en: I emerged from it feeling scared and overwhelmed and devastated by what I'd seen and by the reality that suffering is not just unjustly distributed but fundamentally unjust in the
sentences.zh: 我走出来时感到害怕、不知所措，并被我所见到的景象以及苦难不仅是不公正地分配，而且在本质上就是不公正的现实所摧毁。

sentences.en: fact of it.
sentences.zh: 事实就是如此。

sentences.en: Is there a particular experience from your time at the hospital that maybe set you on a different path?
sentences.zh: 在医院工作期间，有没有哪次特别的经历让你走上了不同的道路？

sentences.en: There was a really bad fire that where I was on call for the fire and it was four kids and two of them died and two of them were very badly burned.
sentences.zh: 有一次非常严重的火灾，我当时负责值班，有四个孩子，其中两个死了，两个被严重烧伤。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's not much to say about that except that trying to be with people in that moment of devastation is difficult.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对此没什么可说的，只是在那种毁灭性的时刻陪伴人们是很困难的。

sentences.en: Obviously, not nearly as difficult as it is to live through, but trying to, you know, support people in that moment is really hard work.
sentences.zh: 显然，这远没有亲身经历那么困难，但试图在那个时刻支持人们确实是一项艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: There is no reason for children to die.
sentences.zh: 孩子们没有理由死亡。

sentences.en: You know, I had a religion professor once who told me there is a law that says that no parent should bury a child and someone needs to enforce it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾经有一位宗教教授告诉我，有一条法律规定没有父母应该埋葬孩子，需要有人来执行它。

sentences.en: And that's how I felt coming out of the hospital.
sentences.zh: 这就是我离开医院时的感受。

sentences.en: Like, there was no one enforcing that law.
sentences.zh: 就像没有人执行那条法律一样。

sentences.en: But a lot of the questions that interested me before the hospital just don't interest me anymore.
sentences.zh: 但在医院之前让我感兴趣的许多问题，现在已经不再让我感兴趣了。

sentences.en: I'm not really interested, for instance, in the question of, like, whether God is really real or whatever.
sentences.zh: 例如，我并不真正关心上帝是否真的存在之类的问题。

sentences.en: The question that's important to me is how can we work together to bring about the world that God, as I understand it, wants us to have?
sentences.zh: 对我来说重要的问题是，我们如何共同努力，实现我所理解的上帝希望我们拥有的世界？

sentences.en: Why does what you just described, why does it not fit within sort of the religious or intellectual purview of being a minister?
sentences.zh: 为什么你刚才描述的内容，不符合作为一名牧师的宗教或知识范畴？

sentences.en: Like, what was the disconnect you felt that precluded you continuing on that path?
sentences.zh: 是什么样的脱节感让你无法继续走那条路？

sentences.en: I'll be honest, there's two things.
sentences.zh: 老实说，有两件事。

sentences.en: So, first off, on a very functional, practical level, I was in a church basement with my mentor, and he was ordering candles out of a catalog.
sentences.zh: 首先，在一个非常功能性、实际的层面上，我和我的导师在教堂地下室，他正在从目录里订购蜡烛。

sentences.en: And I was like, wait a second, this isn't all just, like, worshiping God and, like, helping people and ministering to people.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，等一下，这难道不全是关于崇拜上帝、帮助他人和为人们服务吗？

sentences.en: You have to order candles through a catalog.
sentences.zh: 你还得通过目录订购蜡烛。

sentences.en: And I was like, that's a deal breaker for me.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，这对我来说是不可接受的。

sentences.en: Like, I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我做不到。

sentences.en: And it's, I still have— Because it was too mundane?
sentences.zh: 而且，我仍然有——因为这太世俗了吗？

sentences.en: Or, like, you just didn't—
sentences.zh: 或者，你只是没有——

sentences.en: It's just the kind of thing that I'm bad at, David.
sentences.zh: 这只是我不擅长的那种事情，大卫。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not good at ordering candles.
sentences.zh: 我不擅长订购蜡烛。

sentences.en: And I'm still not good at it.
sentences.zh: 而且我现在依然不擅长。

sentences.en: So that was, like, one thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件事。

sentences.en: But then there was the much deeper kind of philosophical, theological thing, which is that I felt like there were aspects of the liturgy that I would be asked to repeat as
sentences.zh: 但后来还有更深层次的哲学和神学问题，那就是我觉得礼拜仪式中有一些方面，我被要求作为好消息去重复，但我并不确定我是否相信。

sentences.en: good news that I just wasn't sure I believed.
sentences.zh: 好消息，我只是不确定我是否相信。

sentences.en: You know, in thinking about your work and your experiences, again, whether it's in fiction
sentences.zh: 你知道，在思考你的作品和经历时，无论是虚构作品

sentences.en: and, for example, in The Fault in Our Stars, writing about teenagers who are extremely ill, or in your most recent book, Everything is Tuberculosis, writing about global-scale
sentences.zh: 例如在《星运里的错》中，描写身患重病的青少年，或者在你最近的书《一切皆是结核病》中，描写全球规模的

sentences.en: illness, again, they both connect, for me, to the idea of suffering.
sentences.zh: 疾病，对我来说，它们都与苦难的理念相连。

sentences.en: I'm just curious if you feel like you're drawn to suffering.
sentences.zh: 我只是好奇你是否觉得你被苦难所吸引。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm drawn to people who are suffering and trying to make sense of suffering and trying to be with people in a meaningful way who are going through difficulty.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我被那些正在受苦的人所吸引，我试图理解苦难，并试图以一种有意义的方式陪伴那些正在经历困难的人。

sentences.en: I've always felt like that.
sentences.zh: 我一直都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么。

sentences.en: What's your hunch about why you're drawn to it?
sentences.zh: 你觉得为什么会被它吸引？

sentences.en: Well, it's a big deal, for lack of a better term.
sentences.zh: 嗯，用一个词来说，这是一件大事。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, suffering is a big, big deal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，苦难是一件非常非常大的事情。

sentences.en: And it's a huge part of the human experience, and it's a part we often deny or minimize or attempt to look away from.
sentences.zh: 它是人类经验中巨大的一部分，也是我们经常否认、最小化或试图回避的一部分。

sentences.en: And in doing that, I worry that sometimes we deny or minimize or look away from the humanity of people who are suffering.
sentences.zh: 这样做的时候，我担心有时我们否认、最小化或回避了那些正在受苦的人的人性。

sentences.en: And then also, in my own life, I've, you know, known some suffering.
sentences.zh: 而且在我的生活中，我也经历过一些苦难。

sentences.en: I've, you know, I haven't been dying before, but I have been really sick before.
sentences.zh: 我没有濒临死亡，但我以前确实病得很重。

sentences.en: I've been really scared before.
sentences.zh: 我以前真的很害怕。

sentences.en: And so I'm also grappling with it on a personal level.
sentences.zh: 所以我也在个人层面上与它搏斗。

sentences.en: How much do you think one can prepare for suffering?
sentences.zh: 你认为一个人能为苦难做多少准备？

sentences.en: You know, for example, you just described experiencing suffering in your own life.
sentences.zh: 例如，你刚才描述了在你自己的生活中经历苦难。

sentences.en: Did that experience or even your sort of artistic experiences help you with having, for example,
sentences.zh: 那种经历，甚至是你那种艺术上的经历，是否帮助你应对了，例如，

sentences.en: your brother and best friend, Hank, have to deal with a cancer diagnosis a few years ago?
sentences.zh: 你的兄弟兼挚友汉克几年前不得不面对癌症诊断的情况？

sentences.en: Nothing prepared me for Hank getting cancer.
sentences.zh: 没有什么能让我为汉克患癌做好准备。

sentences.en: When I found out he had cancer, before we knew what kind of cancer, which is a terrifying
sentences.zh: 当我发现他患有癌症时，在我们知道是什么癌症之前，那真是令人恐惧的

sentences.en: couple of weeks, I went for this walk through the woods just knowing that being in the forest would calm me down a little bit.
sentences.zh: 几周，我走进树林散步，因为我知道置身于森林会让我平静一点。

sentences.en: And I could barely put one foot in front of the other.
sentences.zh: 我几乎无法迈开脚步。

sentences.en: I remember thinking, you've been with so many people who had this experience, and it has in no way helped you have this experience.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时想，你陪伴过那么多有这种经历的人，但这丝毫没有帮助你应对这种经历。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I don't think it helps, really, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，老实说，我不认为这有什么帮助。

sentences.en: And, you know, if your work and your experiences in no way was able to prepare you for your experience with Hank, who's doing fine right now, is that right?
sentences.zh: 而且，如果你的工作和经历完全无法让你为与汉克的经历做好准备，他现在情况很好，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: I would say better than fine.
sentences.zh: 我会说比很好还要好。

sentences.en: Better than fine.
sentences.zh: 比很好还要好。

sentences.en: It's hard to slow Hank green down, yeah.
sentences.zh: 很难让汉克·格林慢下来，是的。

sentences.en: But if your experience were ultimately ineffectual when it came to your situation with your brother, what do you think the implications of that are for your work generally?
sentences.zh: 但如果你的经验在面对你兄弟的情况时最终是无效的，你认为这对你的工作总体上意味着什么？

sentences.en: Like, is it, how much can it help other people?
sentences.zh: 它能给其他人带来多少帮助？

sentences.en: And how much does it ultimately just have to be about you expressing what you need to express?
sentences.zh: 它最终在多大程度上必须是你表达你需要表达的东西？

sentences.en: Well, I think art does help us feel less alone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为艺术确实能帮助我们感到不那么孤独。

sentences.en: I really believe that.
sentences.zh: 我真的相信这一点。

sentences.en: But I also think that, like, one of the reasons I stopped writing fiction was because I forgot or didn't understand, like, what fiction was for anymore.
sentences.zh: 但我同时也认为，我停止写小说的一个原因是因为我忘记了或者不再理解小说到底是为了什么。

sentences.en: And so, you know, when you write a nonfiction book about tuberculosis, you know exactly what
sentences.zh: 所以，当你写一本关于结核病的非虚构书籍时，你很清楚

sentences.en: you're trying to do, which is raise attention to the fact that 1.5 million people are dying every year of a disease we've known how to cure since the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 你想要做什么，那就是引起人们对这样一个事实的关注：每年有150万人死于一种我们自20世纪50年代以来就知道如何治愈的疾病。

sentences.en: When you're writing fiction, I think the mission is a lot more complex and amorphous and abstract.
sentences.zh: 当你写虚构作品时，我认为使命要复杂、模糊和抽象得多。

sentences.en: When fiction works, for me, it's because I'm also bringing my deepest self to the story just like the writer did.
sentences.zh: 当虚构作品奏效时，对我来说，是因为我也像作者一样，将我最深层的自我带入了故事中。

sentences.en: I'm bringing my own experiences of loss and grief.
sentences.zh: 我带来了我自己的失落和悲伤的经历。

sentences.en: I'm bringing my own joys and hopes to the novel.
sentences.zh: 我将我自己的快乐和希望带入了小说。

sentences.en: And there is a magic in that.
sentences.zh: 其中有一种魔力。

sentences.en: I think fiction can be transformative.
sentences.zh: 我认为虚构作品可以具有变革性。

sentences.en: But I also think that, you know, part of the reason I haven't written a novel in eight years is because I lost track of how that works.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，我八年来没有写过小说，部分原因是我忘记了它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: The way you put it was when I stopped writing fiction.
sentences.zh: 你表达的方式就是当我停止写虚构作品的时候。

sentences.en: Do you mean that definitively?
sentences.zh: 你是认真的吗？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是。

sentences.en: In fact, I'm writing fiction now.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我现在正在写小说。

sentences.en: So what were some of the things that you lost track of?
sentences.zh: 那么，有哪些事情是你无法掌控的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So I wasn't sure what role that my novels could play in the moment in which I found myself,
sentences.zh: 所以我当时并不确定，在那种境况下，我的小说能起到什么作用，

sentences.en: you know, starting in 2018.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是2018年开始的时候。

sentences.en: Another factor for sure is that lots of readers were inevitably reading me into my stories.
sentences.zh: 另一个肯定的因素是，很多读者不可避免地把我和我的故事联系在一起。

sentences.en: And that was very uncomfortable and difficult for me and hard for me to navigate.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常不舒服、困难，也很难应对。

sentences.en: I mean, I wrote a novel about a girl with OCD.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我写了一本关于患有强迫症女孩的小说。

sentences.en: I also have OCD.
sentences.zh: 我也有强迫症。

sentences.en: Navigating the distance between that girl and me became very complicated and fraught in a world where everyone assumed that my OCD was identical to A's as OCD.
sentences.zh: 在一个每个人都认为我的强迫症和书中女孩的强迫症一模一样的世界里，处理我和那个女孩之间的距离变得非常复杂且令人焦虑。

sentences.en: So you wrote The Fault in Our Stars in 2012.
sentences.zh: 所以你在2012年写了《星运里的错》。

sentences.en: And then that book wasn't just a bestseller, which would have been a dream come true for any author.
sentences.zh: 那本书不仅仅是一本畅销书，这对任何作家来说都是梦想成真。

sentences.en: It was sort of this world-eating mega bestseller.
sentences.zh: 它简直是一本风靡全球的超级畅销书。

sentences.en: The numbers I've seen are like 20 million copies sold or something like completely wild like that,
sentences.zh: 我看到的数字是卖出了两千万册左右，简直疯狂至极，

sentences.en: which I think is a level of success, like way beyond what any writer who's not like a crazy egomaniac can reasonably expect.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种成功程度，远远超出了任何一个不是疯狂自大狂的作家所能合理预期的。

sentences.en: How did that level of success change how you think about what you could do moving forward?
sentences.zh: 这种程度的成功如何改变了你对未来创作方向的思考？

sentences.en: Well, on the one hand, it offered me a tremendous amount of freedom because The Fault in Our Stars was so successful that I didn't need to write another book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一方面，它给了我巨大的自由，因为《星运里的错》太成功了，我不需要再写另一本书。

sentences.en: I was able to write exactly the book I wanted exactly when I wanted.
sentences.zh: 我可以随心所欲地在任何时候写我想写的书。

sentences.en: So on that level, it was wonderful.
sentences.zh: 所以从那个层面来说，这很棒。

sentences.en: And then it was also wonderful on the level of reaching so many readers and having readers
sentences.zh: 而且在触达如此多读者，并得到读者

sentences.en: respond so generously to the book and, you know, share it with their friends and their parents and their kids and, but there's another level at which it's, it's difficult.
sentences.zh: 慷慨回应的层面上，这也非常美妙，你知道，他们把书分享给朋友、父母和孩子，但另一方面，它也确实很困难。

sentences.en: You know, when you're up near the center of U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你处于美国流行文化的中心附近时，

sentences.en: pop culture, it's not an entirely pleasant experience, at least for me.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一种完全愉快的体验，至少对我来说是这样。

sentences.en: It's sort of like being at the top of a mountain where there isn't much oxygen.
sentences.zh: 这就像站在氧气稀薄的山顶上一样。

sentences.en: I wanted to get off the top of the mountain pretty quickly, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我当时很想尽快从山顶下来。

sentences.en: And, um, yeah, it, parts of it were really difficult.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，是的，它，其中一些部分真的很难。

sentences.en: Parts of it were really hard.
sentences.zh: 有些部分真的很难熬。

sentences.en: You know, we had to move, like people would come to our house.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们不得不搬家，因为人们会找上门来。

sentences.en: Lots of things in our lives changed that we didn't necessarily want to have changed.
sentences.zh: 我们生活中很多事情都改变了，而这些改变未必是我们想要的。

sentences.en: But looking back, I feel nothing but gratitude for that experience because the book has reached
sentences.zh: 但回首往事，我除了感激还是感激，因为这本书触动了

sentences.en: so many people and it's given me lots of opportunities that I could never have dreamt of.
sentences.zh: 如此多的人，它给了我许多我从未梦想过的机会。

sentences.en: I want to, uh, just briefly move to an idea that's connected more to, uh, everything is tuberculosis, which, you know, of course is not just about tuberculosis.
sentences.zh: 我想，呃，简要谈谈一个与《一切皆是结核病》更相关的话题，你知道，这当然不仅仅是关于结核病。

sentences.en: It's also about global health.
sentences.zh: 它也关乎全球健康。

sentences.en: You know, it's undeniable that the, the Trump administration in various ways has pulled back from aiding global health.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不可否认的是，特朗普政府在各方面都减少了对全球健康的援助。

sentences.en: And I think there are all sorts of, um, to varying degrees of plausibility, all sorts of political or, or economic arguments that could be made for why the Trump administration is,
sentences.zh: 我认为有各种各样的，嗯，在不同程度上看似合理的，各种各样的政治或经济论点可以用来解释为什么特朗普政府在，

sentences.en: you know, dismantling USAID.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拆解美国国际开发署（USAID）。

sentences.en: How do you understand the Trump administration's moral or philosophical attitude when it comes to making moves like that?
sentences.zh: 当你面对这样的举动时，你是如何理解特朗普政府的道德或哲学态度的？

sentences.en: I was talking to a friend not that long ago about this same subject and his attitude was, that's what evil is.
sentences.zh: 不久前我和一位朋友谈论过同样的话题，他的态度是，这就是邪恶。

sentences.en: Now, to my mind, that's maybe, uh, an exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 现在，在我看来，这可能，呃，是一种夸大。

sentences.en: I don't know if I understand it as evil, but like, how do you understand the decision to make moves that result in more suffering?
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否将其理解为邪恶，但你如何理解那些导致更多苦难的决策？

sentences.en: Where do you think it comes from?
sentences.zh: 你认为这源于什么？

sentences.en: What motivates it?
sentences.zh: 是什么动机驱使的？

sentences.en: Well, I, I would say that the belief that some human lives have more value than others is the root of all evil.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会说，认为某些人的生命比其他人更有价值的信念是万恶之源。

sentences.en: And this is clearly an expression of that belief.
sentences.zh: 而这显然就是那种信念的表达。

sentences.en: If I don't understand it, I guess I understand it as a belief that the United States, with its limited resources, should focus on the needs of the United States.
sentences.zh: 如果我不理解它，我想我把它理解为一种信念，即美国应该利用其有限的资源，专注于美国自身的需求。

sentences.en: But that is such a narrow-minded way to think about how the United States became the country that it has become in terms of its power, in terms of its relative wealth, in terms of
sentences.zh: 但这是一种极其狭隘的思维方式，去思考美国是如何成为今天这个国家的，就其力量而言，就其相对财富而言，就其

sentences.en: its, um, ability to, um, have some say in what happens in the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在世界事务中拥有一定话语权的能力而言。

sentences.en: If you want to take a sort of traditional conservative approach to it, it's the best use of soft power that the United States has ever had.
sentences.zh: 如果你想采取一种传统的保守主义方法，这是美国有史以来对软实力的最佳利用。

sentences.en: If you want to take a moral philosophical approach to it, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果你想采取一种道德哲学的方法，美国

sentences.en: is directly responsible for saving tens of millions of lives through PEPFAR.
sentences.zh: 通过“总统防治艾滋病紧急救援计划”（PEPFAR）直接拯救了数千万人的生命。

sentences.en: It's support of the Global Fund and USAID.
sentences.zh: 这是对全球基金和美国国际开发署的支持。

sentences.en: And so it's something that traditionally, I think, Americans have had real cause to feel proud about.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，传统上美国人确实有理由为此感到自豪。

sentences.en: The dismantling of USAID, the questions around support for the Global Fund, the questions around support for PEPFAR, it's just devastating.
sentences.zh: 拆解美国国际开发署，围绕支持全球基金的质疑，围绕支持PEPFAR的质疑，这简直是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: And so for me, I guess to be honest, like, I can't look back because if I look back, I feel such grief and such anger.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，老实说，我无法回首过去，因为如果我回首，我会感到如此悲伤和愤怒。

sentences.en: I can only look forward and try to say, okay, well, given the world in which we now live, what can we do together?
sentences.zh: 我只能向前看，试着说，好吧，鉴于我们现在所处的世界，我们能一起做些什么？

sentences.en: I want to turn now to the subject of YouTube and the work you do there.
sentences.zh: 现在我想转向YouTube以及你在那里所做的工作这个话题。

sentences.en: You know, there's all sorts of evidence that social media and watching videos and living online is bad for young people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有各种证据表明社交媒体、观看视频和生活在网络上对年轻人是有害的。

sentences.en: I think there's very little evidence that it's good for them.
sentences.zh: 我认为几乎没有证据表明它对他们有益。

sentences.en: Do you have any ambivalence about participating in an ecosystem that might just generally not be good for kids and teens?
sentences.zh: 对于参与一个可能对儿童和青少年总体上并不好的生态系统，你是否感到矛盾？

sentences.en: Yeah, I made a video a while back called Am I Cigarettes, where I wondered if just by creating content on the social internet, I might be a sort of form of tobacco consumption.
sentences.zh: 是的，我很久以前做过一个视频叫《我是香烟吗？》，我在其中怀疑，仅仅通过在社交网络上创作内容，我可能是一种烟草消费形式。

sentences.en: I do have a lot of ambivalence about it, and I go back and forth on it a lot.
sentences.zh: 我对此确实感到非常矛盾，并且经常反复思考。

sentences.en: There have been years where I really didn't use the social internet except for YouTube.
sentences.zh: 有几年我除了YouTube之外，真的没有使用过社交网络。

sentences.en: And then there have been years where I used it a lot.
sentences.zh: 后来又有几年我使用得很多。

sentences.en: And the years where I didn't use it much were happier years for me.
sentences.zh: 而我不怎么使用它的那几年，是我更快乐的时光。

sentences.en: Where did you land on the question of am I cigarettes?
sentences.zh: 关于“我是香烟吗”这个问题，你得出了什么结论？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I came out of that video quite unsure as to whether I'm cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，拍完那个视频后，我还是很不确定自己是否是香烟。

sentences.en: My brother then made a follow-up video where he was like, we're food, and there's a lot of bad food out there, but hopefully we're good food.
sentences.zh: 我弟弟后来做了一个后续视频，他说，我们是食物，外面有很多垃圾食品，但希望我们是健康的食物。

sentences.en: And I thought that was a good point.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: I think that abandoning the space is probably the wrong response.
sentences.zh: 我认为放弃这个空间可能不是正确的应对方式。

sentences.en: I do think that YouTube has become a really productive place to share educational resources to lower barriers to educational access for people.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为YouTube已经成为一个分享教育资源、降低人们获取教育门槛的非常有成效的地方。

sentences.en: And so I feel less ambivalence about using that space.
sentences.zh: 所以我对使用那个空间感到没那么矛盾了。

sentences.en: And our particular community, I think, is really important for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们这个特定的社区对很多人来说真的很重要。

sentences.en: It's really, it's a big part of their identity.
sentences.zh: 它确实，它是他们身份认同的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: And I think the work we do together is useful and important.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们一起做的工作是有用且重要的。

sentences.en: In the nonfiction book that you published before everything is tuberculosis, the Anthropocene
sentences.zh: 在你出版《一切皆是结核病》之前的非虚构类书籍中，《人类世》

sentences.en: Reviewed.
sentences.zh: 《评论》。

sentences.en: Yeah, what a title.
sentences.zh: 是的，多好的书名啊。

sentences.en: Can you pronounce that word more smoothly than I can?
sentences.zh: 你能比我更顺畅地读出那个词吗？

sentences.en: I mean, only via practice.
sentences.zh: 我是说，只能通过练习。

sentences.en: Wait, say it right now.
sentences.zh: 等等，现在读一遍。

sentences.en: Anthropocene.
sentences.zh: 人类世（Anthropocene）。

sentences.en: Oh, that was much better.
sentences.zh: 哦，那好多了。

sentences.en: You know, the book consists of, it's short essays where you review all sorts of things in the world and then at the end, give them a star rating.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这本书由短篇散文组成，你评论了世界上各种各样的事物，最后给它们打星级评分。

sentences.en: And one of the reviews is of the internet, which you gave a rating of three out of five stars.
sentences.zh: 其中一篇评论是关于互联网的，你给了它五星中的三星。

sentences.en: And at the end of that review, that essay, you ask a bunch of rhetorical questions, including
sentences.zh: 在那篇评论，也就是那篇文章的结尾，你问了一连串反问句，包括

sentences.en: what does it mean to have my way of thinking and my way of being so profoundly shaped by machine logic?
sentences.zh: 我的思维方式和存在方式被机器逻辑如此深刻地塑造，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: What does it mean that having been part of the internet for so long, the internet is also part of me?
sentences.zh: 在互联网上待了这么久，互联网也成为了我的一部分，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: I want to know your answers to those questions.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你对这些问题的回答。

sentences.en: What happens to you when the internet becomes a big part of who you are and what you do?
sentences.zh: 当互联网成为你个人和你所做之事的重要组成部分时，你会发生什么？

sentences.en: I think the easy answer is that the internet, when the internet becomes part of you, you cede a certain amount of your overall sense of self to online experience, which can be
sentences.zh: 我认为简单的答案是，当互联网成为你的一部分时，你会将一部分整体的自我感让渡给在线体验，这在某些方面可能

sentences.en: wonderful in some ways, right?
sentences.zh: 很美妙，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I mean, how else, you know, I was, this is going to surprise you, David, but I was a big nerd when I was a kid and I would have loved...
sentences.zh: 比如，我是说，不然还能怎样，你知道，我，这会让你感到惊讶，大卫，但我小时候是个大书呆子，我本来会很喜欢……

sentences.en: I had you pegged for captain of the football team.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为你是橄榄球队队长。

sentences.en: I would have loved to be able to connect with young people the way that young people can
sentences.zh: 我本来会很喜欢能够像现在的年轻人那样，

sentences.en: connect with each other now across time and space around shared affinities or shared interests, right?
sentences.zh: 围绕共同的爱好或兴趣，跨越时间和空间与彼此建立联系，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it would have been amazing for me to have a relationship with other people who were obsessed with collecting every version of the 1986 Chicago Cubs baseball cards.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果能和其他痴迷于收集1986年芝加哥小熊队棒球卡每一个版本的人建立联系，那对我来说太棒了。

sentences.en: The internet has facilitated communication in lots of really beautiful ways.
sentences.zh: 互联网以许多非常美妙的方式促进了交流。

sentences.en: And then there is the coSt.
sentences.zh: 然后就是代价。

sentences.en: And I feel like I have lived both sides of that coin.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我亲历了这枚硬币的两面。

sentences.en: But tell me, tell me more about how you've lived both sides of that coin.
sentences.zh: 但告诉我，多告诉我一些关于你如何亲历这枚硬币两面的经历。

sentences.en: Well, you weren't on Tumblr in 2012 when Tumblr loved me, but you also weren't on Tumblr in
sentences.zh: 嗯，2012年Tumblr喜欢我的时候你不在上面，但2014年Tumblr没那么喜欢我的时候，

sentences.en: 2014 when Tumblr didn't love me as much, is what I guess I would say.
sentences.zh: 你也不在上面，我想我会这么说。

sentences.en: What was going on in 2014?
sentences.zh: 2014年发生了什么？

sentences.en: Just a lot of, like, bad faith interpretations of my work, I would say.
sentences.zh: 只是有很多，比如，对我作品的恶意解读，我会这么说。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Was any of that illuminating?
sentences.zh: 其中有什么启发吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think with the rise of YouTube and social media, you know, that's also resulted in a rise in young people wanting to be on YouTube and obviously on social media.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为随着YouTube和社交媒体的兴起，你知道，这也导致了年轻人想要上YouTube以及显然是社交媒体的愿望的增长。

sentences.en: And is there something that you, as a public figure, wish that teens understood about what it means to put yourself out there publicly?
sentences.zh: 作为一个公众人物，你是否希望青少年们能理解在公共场合展示自己意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, I understand the urge to have outside affirmation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我理解那种渴望获得外界认可的冲动。

sentences.en: I think that's something we all have.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们所有人都有的东西。

sentences.en: And I think when we're young, we have it perhaps most profoundly.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为当我们年轻时，这种渴望或许最为强烈。

sentences.en: I know that when I was a teenager, I wanted to be known and loved.
sentences.zh: 我知道当我还是个青少年时，我渴望被了解和被爱。

sentences.en: And being famous on the internet feels like a wonderful shortcut to that.
sentences.zh: 而在互联网上出名感觉就像是实现这一目标的绝佳捷径。

sentences.en: It feels like everyone knows you and everyone loves you, but in fact, no one knows you.
sentences.zh: 感觉好像每个人都认识你，每个人都爱你，但事实上，没有人真正了解你。

sentences.en: So I think there's a lot to recommend making stuff online for people.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为人们在网上创作内容有很多值得推荐的地方。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它。

sentences.en: I'm very grateful that I get to do it every week.
sentences.zh: 我非常感激我每周都能做这件事。

sentences.en: I've been doing it every week since 2007.
sentences.zh: 从2007年起，我每周都在做这件事。

sentences.en: I want to do it every week for as long as I can do it in a way that feels productive and helpful.
sentences.zh: 只要我能以一种感觉有成效且有帮助的方式去做，我就想每周都做下去。

sentences.en: I also think that the feeling that somehow being famous or achieving 100,000 subscribers or a million subscribers or whatever number of subscribers feels like it will fill the
sentences.zh: 我也认为那种觉得出名或者获得十万订阅者、一百万订阅者，或者无论多少订阅者，就能填补你内心空洞的感觉，

sentences.en: hole inside of you, it will not.
sentences.zh: 是不会奏效的。

sentences.en: There is no filling the hole inside of you with the internet.
sentences.zh: 用互联网是无法填补你内心的空洞的。

sentences.en: Well, I don't want to say that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不想这么说。

sentences.en: That's not always true.
sentences.zh: 那并不总是真的。

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 那是个好问题。

sentences.en: Let me think about how to answer it more honestly.
sentences.zh: 让我思考一下如何更诚实地回答它。

sentences.en: I think there's a lot to recommend about being a YouTuber, but I also think that being famous, especially when you're young, is really disorienting.
sentences.zh: 我认为做一名YouTuber有很多值得推荐的地方，但我也认为出名，尤其是当你年轻的时候，真的会让人迷失方向。

sentences.en: What were you saying in your answer that felt dishonest?
sentences.zh: 你在回答中说了什么让你觉得不诚实？

sentences.en: Just that I don't know what it's like to get famous when I'm 16, and so it's not my job to preach to them.
sentences.zh: 只是我不知道16岁成名是什么感觉，所以教导他们不是我的工作。

sentences.en: In a couple ways, we've touched on the subject of anxiety, and it's, well, I mean, the success of Jonathan Haidt's book, right?
sentences.zh: 在几个方面，我们触及了焦虑这个话题，而且，嗯，我是说，乔纳森·海特那本书的成功，对吧？

sentences.en: The Anxious Generation, I think, speaks to a real feeling that our kids are more anxious than they used to be.
sentences.zh: 《焦虑的一代》，我认为这反映了一种真实的感受，即我们的孩子比过去更焦虑了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I was anxious way before they were.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我早在他们之前就很焦虑了。

sentences.en: Well, and so this is related to my question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这与我的问题有关。

sentences.en: As someone who has really struggled with anxiety, and I'm sure you get these kinds of questions,
sentences.zh: 作为一个真正与焦虑斗争过的人，我相信你经常遇到这类问题，

sentences.en: but what do you say to young people when they want to know how to try to reduce or manage anxiety?
sentences.zh: 但当年轻人想知道如何尝试减少或管理焦虑时，你会对他们说什么？

sentences.en: It's really hard.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难。

sentences.en: I mean, living with intense anxiety is the hardest thing I've ever done.
sentences.zh: 我是说，带着强烈的焦虑生活是我做过最难的事情。

sentences.en: It's really hard.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难。

sentences.en: And I think that's the first thing, is acknowledging that it's really hard, and that acknowledging that surviving it is itself a win.
sentences.zh: 我认为首先要做的是承认这真的很难，并且承认能够挺过来本身就是一种胜利。

sentences.en: I find going outside helpful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得去户外走走很有帮助。

sentences.en: I find exercise helpful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得锻炼很有帮助。

sentences.en: I find, even though it makes me anxious in the short run, I find being with other people helpful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，尽管短期内会让我感到焦虑，但我发现与他人在一起很有帮助。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of the things that make me feel less anxious in the moment make me feel more anxious in the long run.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多让我当下感觉不那么焦虑的事情，从长远来看反而让我更焦虑。

sentences.en: So if I'm at a party, I'm already anxious, because who wants to go to a party?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我在聚会上，我已经很焦虑了，因为谁想去参加聚会呢？

sentences.en: But I sometimes will deal with that anxiety by, like, getting on my phone.
sentences.zh: 但我有时会通过玩手机来应对那种焦虑。

sentences.en: And that makes me feel better in the moment, but it actually makes me feel worse in the long run.
sentences.zh: 这让我当下感觉好些了，但从长远来看，它实际上让我感觉更糟。

sentences.en: You mean being on your phone at the party?
sentences.zh: 你是说在聚会上玩手机吗？

sentences.en: At the party, yeah.
sentences.zh: 在派对上，没错。

sentences.en: What makes me feel better in the long run is engaging with other human beings as I find them, even though that causes me more initial anxiety.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，让我感觉更好的是去接触我所遇到的其他人，尽管这在初期会让我感到更焦虑。

sentences.en: And so I've learned over the years to try to do that stuff, to take my medication every day, to do all the stuff that I'm supposed to do, the stuff that science says works.
sentences.zh: 所以多年来我学会了尝试去做那些事，每天按时服药，做所有我应该做的事，做那些科学证明有效的事。

sentences.en: But it's still really hard.
sentences.zh: 但这依然非常困难。

sentences.en: Like, I mean, you know, I'm fairly anxious now, because this is a weird circumstance.
sentences.zh: 比如，我是说，你知道，我现在相当焦虑，因为这是一种奇怪的情况。

sentences.en: Um, but I'll be much more anxious when it is over, because I'll be hyperanalyzing everything I said and everything I didn't say, and yada, yada, yada.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但当这一切结束时我会更加焦虑，因为我会过度剖析我说的每一句话和没说的每一句话，诸如此类，等等。

sentences.en: So it's funny, because anytime things are good, and things are relatively good right now, I understand that that's temporary.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣，因为每当事情进展顺利时——现在情况相对不错——我明白那只是暂时的。

sentences.en: And then when things are bad, that feels very permanent.
sentences.zh: 而当事情变得糟糕时，那种感觉却非常持久。

sentences.en: Like when I'm dealing with really high anxiety every day, it feels like that's going to be forever.
sentences.zh: 就像我每天都在应对极度焦虑时，感觉那好像会永远持续下去。

sentences.en: Or if I'm dealing with major depression, it feels like that's going to be forever.
sentences.zh: 或者如果我正处于严重的抑郁中，也会觉得那将永无止境。

sentences.en: So it's easy for me to tell myself it's temporary when things are good.
sentences.zh: 所以当一切顺利时，我很容易告诉自己这只是暂时的。

sentences.en: It's really hard to remind myself that it's temporary when things are bad.
sentences.zh: 但当情况糟糕时，要提醒自己这只是暂时的就非常困难了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It can feel like an unfortunate quirk of evolution that our brains can, I think, tend to fixate
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是进化带来的一个不幸的怪癖，我认为，我们的大脑往往更倾向于专注于威胁，

sentences.en: on threats much more than they're likely to fixate on, you know, possible positive things.
sentences.zh: 而不是专注于那些可能的积极事物。

sentences.en: I often think about what it would be like to be a different mammal, and how then I would also be always responding to threats.
sentences.zh: 我经常思考成为另一种哺乳动物会是什么样子，以及那时我是否也会总是对威胁做出反应。

sentences.en: Like if I was a squirrel, I would also be in a constant state of worry and fear.
sentences.zh: 比如如果我是一只松鼠，我也会处于持续的担忧和恐惧之中。

sentences.en: And that worry and fear would be completely justified, just as my current worry and fear is, like, I'm right to be afraid of dying.
sentences.zh: 而那种担忧和恐惧是完全合理的，就像我现在的担忧和恐惧一样，比如，我害怕死亡是正确的。

sentences.en: Like, I am going to die.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我终将一死。

sentences.en: And that is a super weird thing to have happen to a being with a consciousness.
sentences.zh: 对于一个有意识的生命来说，这真是一件超级奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not wrong to be panicked the same way that, like, squirrels aren't wrong to be panicked when they're crossing the street.
sentences.zh: 所以，我感到恐慌并没有错，就像松鼠在过马路时感到恐慌并没有错一样。

sentences.en: It just doesn't happen to be helpful.
sentences.zh: 只是这没什么帮助罢了。

sentences.en: How did, um, or how has being a parent affected your own anxieties?
sentences.zh: 那么，嗯，或者说，为人父母对你自己的焦虑有什么影响吗？

sentences.en: Pretty profoundly.
sentences.zh: 相当深远。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there's the old cliche that your heart beats outside of your chest, and that's true in some ways.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，有句老话叫“你的心跳在你的胸腔之外”，在某些方面确实如此。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I worry intensely for my kids.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我为我的孩子们感到极度担忧。

sentences.en: It's impossible not to.
sentences.zh: 这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: I, um, I've never had a job so interesting, and I've never had a job so hard as being a parent.
sentences.zh: 我，嗯，我从未做过如此有趣的工作，也从未做过像为人父母这样艰难的工作。

sentences.en: Have your kids read your books?
sentences.zh: 你的孩子们读过你的书吗？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有。

sentences.en: And I don't think they have any interest in it.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得他们对此毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: I mean, I didn't care what my dad did when I was a kid, and I don't think they care much what their dad does, and that's, that suits me just fine.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我小时候也不关心我爸爸是做什么的，我觉得他们也不太关心他们爸爸做什么，这对我来说挺好的。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我懂。

sentences.en: It's pretty great.
sentences.zh: 这挺棒的。

sentences.en: It's humbling, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这让人感到谦卑，不是吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是啊。

sentences.en: And, like, but, like, I mean, why would they?
sentences.zh: 而且，就像，但是，我是说，他们为什么要关心呢？

sentences.en: Like, I mean, I don't, uh, you know, I, um, I knew what my dad's job was, but I didn't think about him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不，呃，你知道，我，嗯，我知道我爸爸的工作是什么，但我不会去想他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, the whole point of having a good dad is that you don't have to think about them very much.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拥有一个好爸爸的全部意义就在于你不需要过多地去想他们。

sentences.en: Just, just be there.
sentences.zh: 只要，只要在场就好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Um, this is a tangential thing, but I think it was in the New Yorker profile of you from almost 10 years ago, something like that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个题外话，但我记得那是差不多十年前《纽约客》对你的一篇人物专访，大概是那样。

sentences.en: The writer was writing about how you were studying creative writing in college, and you had an experience where you read a story in class that had a sex scene in it,
sentences.zh: 作者写到你在大学学习创意写作，有一次你在课堂上读了一个包含性爱场景的故事，

sentences.en: and then your professor said, I guess in front of the whole class, you've never had sex before, have you?
sentences.zh: 然后你的教授说，我想是在全班同学面前，你以前从没做过爱，对吧？

sentences.en: Do you remember the anecdote that I'm talking about?
sentences.zh: 你还记得我说的那段轶事吗？

sentences.en: Barely.
sentences.zh: 几乎不记得了。

sentences.en: I haven't told that story in a long time.
sentences.zh: 我已经很久没讲过那个故事了。

sentences.en: I completely forgot that was in The New Yorker.
sentences.zh: 我完全忘了那件事被写进了《纽约客》里。

sentences.en: How horrifying.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: But, you know, of course, the professor, you know, you said he was right.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当然，那位教授，你知道，你说他是对的。

sentences.en: Yeah, he was.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是对的。

sentences.en: Do you remember what gave it away?
sentences.zh: 你记得是什么让他看出来的吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不记得。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't remember at all.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我完全不记得了。

sentences.en: Probably just a general romanticization of sexuality, I would imagine, but I have no idea what gave it away.
sentences.zh: 我想大概只是对性的一种普遍的浪漫化想象吧，但我完全不知道是什么让他看出来的。

sentences.en: That's really funny, though.
sentences.zh: 不过那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was—I remember that class.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那是——我记得那节课。

sentences.en: I had a great teacher, and he did say that in front of the whole class.
sentences.zh: 我有一位很棒的老师，他确实在全班同学面前说了那句话。

sentences.en: But then apparently you used to give class updates on, like, your progress on that problem.
sentences.zh: 但后来听说你还会在课堂上更新你在这个问题上的进展。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Did I really?
sentences.zh: 我真的这么做了吗？

sentences.en: That's what's in the story.
sentences.zh: 故事里就是这么写的。

sentences.en: I thought—
sentences.zh: 我以为——

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: You're making me feel like I'm folding into a series of increasingly small polygons until I just disappear.
sentences.zh: 你让我感觉自己正在折叠成一系列越来越小的多边形，直到我彻底消失。

sentences.en: I'm just wondering, like, who was this guy?
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，这家伙到底是谁？

sentences.en: Who was that—
sentences.zh: 那个人是谁——

sentences.en: Who was that guy?
sentences.zh: 那个人是谁？

sentences.en: Who was that man at that point in his life where he—
sentences.zh: 那个男人在他生命中的那个阶段，他竟然——

sentences.en: Oh, David, thank God we all have the capacity for change and growth.
sentences.zh: 哦，David，谢天谢地，我们都有改变和成长的能力。

sentences.en: No, I don't remember that at all.
sentences.zh: 不，我完全不记得了。

sentences.en: I mean, I remember not having had sex in college, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我确实记得大学时没做过爱。

sentences.en: But I don't remember—
sentences.zh: 但我完全不记得——

sentences.en: Talking about it in class.
sentences.zh: 在课堂上谈论这件事。

sentences.en: I don't remember that at all.
sentences.zh: 我完全不记得了。

sentences.en: I don't remember talking about it in class, and I'm duly horrified by the fact that I did.
sentences.zh: 我不记得在课堂上谈论过它，而且对于我居然真的这么做了，我感到非常羞愧。

sentences.en: Because my thing was, I would—you know, the idea of—even the idea of that seems absolutely mortifying to me.
sentences.zh: 因为我的原则是，我会——你知道，那种想法——即使是那种想法对我来说都绝对令人难堪。

sentences.en: So I was trying to understand who was the person who would have done that willingly.
sentences.zh: 所以我试图理解那个会心甘情愿做这种事的人到底是谁。

sentences.en: Also a little bit incongruous with the person I believe myself to be, you know?
sentences.zh: 而且这和我自认为的那个人有点不符，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Like, which is a funny thing.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Like, as we get older, the stories we tell about ourselves change, of course.
sentences.zh: 就像，随着年龄增长，我们讲述的关于自己的故事当然会改变。

sentences.en: And, you know, when I was young, I told one set of stories about myself.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当我年轻的时候，我讲述了一套关于我自己的故事。

sentences.en: And now, like, when I tell some of those stories, I'm always like,
sentences.zh: 现在，当我讲述其中一些故事时，我总是会觉得，

sentences.en: Ugh, no, I don't like that story at all.
sentences.zh: 呃，不，我一点也不喜欢那个故事。

sentences.en: Like, I don't like that guy.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不喜欢那个家伙。

sentences.en: And what do you think the story you're telling about yourself now is?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得你现在讲述的关于自己的故事是什么？

sentences.en: Just a dad in Indianapolis, man.
sentences.zh: 就是一个在印第安纳波利斯的爸爸，伙计。

sentences.en: Like, just a—
sentences.zh: 就像，只是一个——

sentences.en: Don't give me that.
sentences.zh: 别跟我来这一套。

sentences.en: Don't—no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 别——不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the story—
sentences.zh: 我是说，那就是那个故事——

sentences.en: No, no, just a dad in Indianapolis.
sentences.zh: 不，不，就是一个在印第安纳波利斯的爸爸。

sentences.en: That's the story I'm trying to tell, whether or not it's real or not.
sentences.zh: 这就是我试图讲述的故事，不管它是不是真的。

sentences.en: After the break, John and I talk again about why he's so drawn to writing about young people.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，John和我将再次探讨为什么他如此热衷于描写年轻人。

sentences.en: The first embrace of those feelings is just so intense.
sentences.zh: 对那些情感的初次拥抱是如此强烈。

sentences.en: It's so overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 它是如此令人难以抗拒。

sentences.en: There's no irony to it.
sentences.zh: 其中没有任何讽刺意味。

sentences.en: There's no emotional distance between you and it.
sentences.zh: 你和它之间没有任何情感距离。

sentences.en: There is only the reality of experience.
sentences.zh: 只有体验的真实性。

sentences.en: And I think in my fiction, I do want to go back to that.
sentences.zh: 我想在我的小说中，我确实想回到那种状态。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是Winnalou。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: John, thanks for taking the time to talk with me again.
sentences.zh: John，谢谢你抽出时间再次与我交谈。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, it's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 没关系，这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: When we were talking earlier, you said that, I think it was around 2018 was the year you
sentences.zh: 我们之前交谈时，你说过，我想大概是在2018年左右，你

sentences.en: pointed to as being a time when you became unsure of what role novels could play in that moment.
sentences.zh: 指出那是你开始不确定小说在那个时刻能发挥什么作用的时期。

sentences.en: My novels.
sentences.zh: 我的小说。

sentences.en: Your novels.
sentences.zh: 你的小说。

sentences.en: Your novels.
sentences.zh: 你的小说。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Other people's novels.
sentences.zh: 别人的小说。

sentences.en: Very useful to me.
sentences.zh: 对我很有用。

sentences.en: What was going on in that moment that caused that uncertainty for you?
sentences.zh: 当时发生了什么导致你产生了那种不确定感？

sentences.en: Well, I think some of it was the first Trump administration, a feeling that certain aspects of American life that I'd taken for granted were not to be taken for granted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想部分原因是特朗普政府的初期，一种感觉是，我一直认为理所当然的美国生活的某些方面，其实并非理所当然。

sentences.en: I think some of it was personal, my own lifelong struggle with OCD and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是个人原因，我一生都在与强迫症和焦虑症作斗争。

sentences.en: When I got home from the Turtles All the Way Down tour, my last novels tour, I became quite sick, both physically.
sentences.zh: 当我结束《海龟无限》的巡回宣传回到家时，我病得很重，身体上也是。

sentences.en: I got this disease called labyrinthitis, but also mental health-wise.
sentences.zh: 我得了迷路炎，但在心理健康方面也出了问题。

sentences.en: And so I think I didn't know how to use my novels or how to use my fiction to respond to that moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我不知道该如何利用我的小说或虚构作品来回应那个时刻。

sentences.en: And then I also think that on some level, I just forgot what my novels were for, like what the point of them was.
sentences.zh: 而且我也觉得在某种程度上，我只是忘记了我的小说是为了什么，比如它们的意义何在。

sentences.en: It started to feel almost like indulgent, I guess, to like just do this fun stuff all the time.
sentences.zh: 我猜，一直做这些有趣的事情开始让我觉得有点放纵了。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I think the truth is that part of it was personal and part of it was just feeling kind of overwhelmed by the prospect of publishing for such a broad audience, to be honest with
sentences.zh: 我认为事实是，部分原因是个人原因，部分原因只是因为面对要为如此广泛的受众出版作品的前景感到不知所措，老实说，

sentences.en: you.
sentences.zh: 对你。

sentences.en: You know, like it's a great gig in a lot of ways and one I'm very grateful for, but it was also overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这在很多方面是一份很棒的工作，我也非常感激，但它也让人感到不知所措。

sentences.en: And you also said that part of the problem with writing fiction back then was that you were feeling like because you had a public life, readers were taking that as sort of an
sentences.zh: 你还说过，当时写小说的问题之一是，你觉得因为你有公众生活，读者们把这当作一种

sentences.en: opportunity to read your work autobiographically, that, you know, you sort of felt maybe uneasy about that.
sentences.zh: 阅读你作品的自传式机会，你知道，你对此感到有些不安。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Have you just decided that's part of the gig now or have you come to terms with that in some way?
sentences.zh: 你现在已经决定这就是工作的一部分了吗，还是说你已经以某种方式接受了这一点？

sentences.en: I think it's part of the gig and it's a good gig, right?
sentences.zh: 我想这是工作的一部分，而且这是一份好工作，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it's easy to focus on the parts of your job that are hard or that are not ideal, but I really like my job.
sentences.zh: 专注于工作中困难或不理想的部分很容易，但我真的很喜欢我的工作。

sentences.en: There are aspects of my job I like less.
sentences.zh: 我的工作中也有我不那么喜欢的方面。

sentences.en: And that's true for every job I've ever had.
sentences.zh: 我做过的每一份工作都是如此。

sentences.en: Like every job involves paperwork and I hate paperwork.
sentences.zh: 比如每一份工作都涉及文书工作，而我讨厌文书工作。

sentences.en: Or ordering candles.
sentences.zh: 或者订购蜡烛。

sentences.en: Or ordering candles.
sentences.zh: 或者订购蜡烛。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I've tried to find the least paperworky ordering candles jobs possible, but there is still some version of ordering candles in every job.
sentences.zh: 我试着寻找那种最不需要处理文书工作、订购蜡烛的工作，但每一份工作中仍然会有某种形式的“订购蜡烛”的任务。

sentences.en: And I hope that over time, I do think that taking this break from fiction has allowed me to think differently about that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我希望随着时间的推移，我确实认为这段远离虚构创作的休息时间，让我能以不同的方式去思考那些东西。

sentences.en: That like, you know, maybe it's okay that they're going to read me into the story.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，也许他们要把我读进故事里也没关系。

sentences.en: Maybe that's inevitable.
sentences.zh: 也许这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: I read J.D.
sentences.zh: 我读过J.D.

sentences.en: Salinger into Catcher in the Rye, even though he made it very clear he didn't want me to do that.
sentences.zh: 塞林格的《麦田里的守望者》，尽管他明确表示不希望我这样做。

sentences.en: But I still did.
sentences.zh: 但我还是读了。

sentences.en: You know, I still looked for hints of the author in the story.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我还是会在故事里寻找作者的蛛丝马迹。

sentences.en: I just think that's a human impulse.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这是一种人类的本能。

sentences.en: Well, you have some—did you try and send a letter to J.D.
sentences.zh: 那么，你有没有——你有没有试过给J.D.

sentences.en: Salinger at some point?
sentences.zh: 塞林格写信？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我写过。

sentences.en: You remember a lot more of my life than I do, David.
sentences.zh: 你记得我的人生比我还多，大卫。

sentences.en: You've researched it more recently.
sentences.zh: 你最近研究得比较多。

sentences.en: But yeah, I tried to write Salinger a letter.
sentences.zh: 但确实，我试过给塞林格写信。

sentences.en: I read this biography of Salinger in my high school library, and then I tried to—I did.
sentences.zh: 我在高中图书馆读过一本塞林格的传记，然后我就试着——我确实写了。

sentences.en: I wrote him a letter.
sentences.zh: 我给他写了一封信。

sentences.en: I wrote him a letter to like the address that was on the proto-internet, you know, the like CompuServe 1993 internet.
sentences.zh: 我按照那个原始互联网上的地址给他写了信，你知道，就是1993年CompuServe那种互联网。

sentences.en: And, uh, obviously I never got a response, but I felt really compelled to tell him that his book had meant a lot to me.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，显然我从来没收到过回复，但我当时真的很有冲动想告诉他，他的书对我意义重大。

sentences.en: And I don't actually need him to have read that.
sentences.zh: 其实我并不需要他真的读到那封信。

sentences.en: I needed to say it.
sentences.zh: 我只是需要把它说出来。

sentences.en: I don't need him to read it.
sentences.zh: 我不需要他去读。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, whether it's your work in global health or, um, making YouTube videos on any
sentences.zh: 你知道，无论是你在全球健康领域的工作，还是，嗯，在YouTube上制作各种

sentences.en: number of subjects or making podcasts, you're doing a lot of work that is not writing fiction.
sentences.zh: 主题的视频，或者制作播客，你做了很多非虚构写作的工作。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 那是真的。

sentences.en: And I know for myself, like I really think of myself as a writer and I do relatively little writing anymore.
sentences.zh: 我知道对我自己来说，我确实认为自己是一名作家，但我现在做的写作相对较少了。

sentences.en: And I was wondering if how that works for you, given that you're making all this other stuff and like I said, kind of doing less writing than you were doing 15 years ago, 20 years
sentences.zh: 我在想这对你来说是怎么运作的，考虑到你在做所有这些其他的事情，而且正如我所说，你做的写作比15年前、20年前

sentences.en: ago, has your self-conception changed at all?
sentences.zh: 要少，你的自我认知有没有发生变化？

sentences.en: It has changed a little bit, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，确实有一点变化。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I still think of myself as a writer, but I'm conscious of the fact that I, I spend a lot of time not writing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我仍然认为自己是一名作家，但我意识到我花了很多时间在非写作上。

sentences.en: I also always had a day job though.
sentences.zh: 不过我一直都有份日常工作。

sentences.en: So I try to think of it as like, well, I like having a day job.
sentences.zh: 所以我试着这样想，嗯，我喜欢有份日常工作。

sentences.en: Having a day job is good for me.
sentences.zh: 有份日常工作对我来说是件好事。

sentences.en: It's good for my brain.
sentences.zh: 这对我的大脑有好处。

sentences.en: I like not writing all the time.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢不必一直写作。

sentences.en: If writing was the only thing I did, I think I'd put a lot of pressure on myself as a writer,
sentences.zh: 如果写作是我唯一做的事，我想我会给作为作家的自己施加很大的压力，

sentences.en: but I don't think of myself as, as certainly as just a fiction writer anymore.
sentences.zh: 但我不再认为自己仅仅是一名虚构小说作家了。

sentences.en: I mean, I haven't written a novel in almost 10 years, so obviously I'm not primarily a fiction writer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我差不多有10年没写过小说了，所以显然我主要不是一个虚构小说作家。

sentences.en: You also said something along the lines of your fiction tends to work best when you can bring your full self to the story that you're working on.
sentences.zh: 你还说过类似这样的话，即当你能将完整的自我投入到正在创作的故事中时，你的虚构作品往往效果最好。

sentences.en: And I thought, like, why is it that you think you're able to bring your full self to the writing of YA fiction in particular?
sentences.zh: 我就在想，你为什么认为自己能够将完整的自我投入到青少年小说的创作中呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think that for me, my own teenage years were so important because so many things happened for the first time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为对我来说，我自己的青少年时期非常重要，因为很多事情都是第一次发生。

sentences.en: I lost a friend for the first time.
sentences.zh: 我第一次失去了朋友。

sentences.en: And so that meant grappling, not just with grief, but with the unjust distribution of suffering in our world.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我不仅要与悲伤抗争，还要面对世界上苦难分配不公的问题。

sentences.en: I fell in love for the first time, which meant not just the feelings of falling in love,
sentences.zh: 我第一次坠入爱河，这意味着不仅仅是坠入爱河的感觉，

sentences.en: but also the way that it sort of narrows your vision and becomes overwhelmingly the most important thing in your life.
sentences.zh: 还有它会缩小你的视野，让你觉得它是你生命中最重要的事情，这种压倒性的感觉。

sentences.en: I, you know, grappled with the questions of what I owe other people and what I owe myself for the first time, like independent of my parents.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我第一次在父母之外，去思考我亏欠他人什么，又亏欠自己什么的问题。

sentences.en: That time of my life was so important to me.
sentences.zh: 那段时光对我来说太重要了。

sentences.en: It was so, I think partly because I was at boarding school.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是因为我在寄宿学校。

sentences.en: And so I was with my friends all the time, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and my enemies,
sentences.zh: 所以我一直和朋友们在一起，一周七天，一天24小时，还有我的敌人们，

sentences.en: it should be noted, partly because I was the first embrace of those feelings is just so intense.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，部分原因是因为对那些情感的第一次拥抱是如此强烈。

sentences.en: It's so overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 它是如此令人难以抗拒。

sentences.en: There's no irony to it.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何反讽意味。

sentences.en: There's no emotional distance between you and it.
sentences.zh: 你和它之间没有任何情感距离。

sentences.en: There is only the reality of experience.
sentences.zh: 只有体验的真实。

sentences.en: And I think in my fiction, I do want to go back to that.
sentences.zh: 我想在我的虚构作品中，我确实想回到那种状态。

sentences.en: I do want to have that feeling where like, I don't have to have ironic distance between me and the question the way that now I do.
sentences.zh: 我确实想拥有那种感觉，就像我不需要像现在这样，在我和问题之间保持反讽的距离。

sentences.en: You want to get back to the lack of ironic distance.
sentences.zh: 你想回到那种没有反讽距离的状态。

sentences.en: Is that, that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I want to get back to where you look at the stars and you are truly overwhelmed by the size of the universe.
sentences.zh: 我想回到那种当你仰望星空时，会被宇宙的浩瀚所深深震撼的状态。

sentences.en: And for me, that was high school.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那就是高中时期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you think you could approach fiction in the same way and with the same level of emotional intensity if you were writing novels for adults?
sentences.zh: 你认为如果你为成年人写小说，你能以同样的方式和同样的情感强度来处理虚构创作吗？

sentences.en: Well, the novel that I'm working on now is about and for grownups.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我现在正在写的小说就是关于成年人并写给成年人看的。

sentences.en: So I guess we'll see.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们拭目以待吧。

sentences.en: You know, we talked a little bit earlier about faith.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们之前谈到了一点关于信仰的话题。

sentences.en: And you said that you're not really interested in the question of whether God is real.
sentences.zh: 你说你对上帝是否存在的问题并不真正感兴趣。

sentences.en: That really bugs people.
sentences.zh: 这真的很让人生气。

sentences.en: I'm sure it does.
sentences.zh: 我肯定会这样。

sentences.en: But this is the question I have about that.
sentences.zh: 但关于这一点，我有个问题。

sentences.en: So, you know, I've had a couple conversations just in my life with, well, I'm thinking of one in particular with a Catholic prieSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我生活中和人有过几次对话，嗯，我特别想到了一次与一位天主教神父的对话。

sentences.en: And I presented this idea to him that I feel like I can have transcendental or spiritual
sentences.zh: 我向他提出了这个想法，我觉得我可以拥有超验的、精神的

sentences.en: or religious-like experiences without necessarily having to connect them to a belief in a higher power or a God.
sentences.zh: 或类似宗教的体验，而不必非要将它们与对更高力量或上帝的信仰联系起来。

sentences.en: And Father Jonah is his name.
sentences.zh: 他叫乔纳神父。

sentences.en: I'm sure he wouldn't mind me talking about this.
sentences.zh: 我相信他不介意我谈论这件事。

sentences.en: Said very respectfully, like, actually, I kind of think belief in the God is, like, that's the whole deal.
sentences.zh: 他非常恭敬地说，其实，我倒觉得对上帝的信仰，那才是核心所在。

sentences.en: And if you're not there, then you're kind of missing the point.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有达到那个层面，那你其实就错过了重点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How is that not the case?
sentences.zh: 怎么会不是这样呢？

sentences.en: Or why is it not the case for you, I should say?
sentences.zh: 或者我应该问，为什么对你来说不是这样？

sentences.en: Well, I do hear that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实听过这种说法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I do hear that from a lot of theologians.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我确实从很多神学家那里听到过这种说法。

sentences.en: And I think that their experiences of the numinous or the sacred or whatever might be different from mine.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们对神圣、庄严或其他什么的体验可能与我的不同。

sentences.en: And theirs might be contingent upon God being really real, whatever that means.
sentences.zh: 他们的体验可能取决于上帝是否真的存在，无论那意味着什么。

sentences.en: For me, those experiences of the sacred, of God's presence, of God's presence in my life and in the life of the world, they are real.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那些神圣的体验，上帝存在的体验，上帝在我生命中和世界生命中的存在的体验，它们是真实的。

sentences.en: Like, I know that they're real because I have them.
sentences.zh: 就像，我知道它们是真实的，因为我拥有过它们。

sentences.en: And I have them in prayer.
sentences.zh: 我在祈祷时拥有过它们。

sentences.en: I have them when I am overwhelmed by suffering, when I am overwhelmed by fear.
sentences.zh: 当我被苦难淹没时，当我被恐惧淹没时，我拥有过它们。

sentences.en: I have those experiences of the sacred.
sentences.zh: 我拥有过那些神圣的体验。

sentences.en: Whether or not those experiences are constructed by my brain or are experiences of a living God is irrelevant to whether the experience was real for me.
sentences.zh: 无论这些体验是由我的大脑构建的，还是对一位活着的上帝的体验，这与这些体验对我来说是否真实无关。

sentences.en: And so what I'm interested in is, like, how do I get more of that experience, that experience
sentences.zh: 所以我感兴趣的是，我该如何获得更多那样的体验，那种

sentences.en: of feeling proximal to the sacred, that experience of feeling close to a justice-loving
sentences.zh: 感觉与神圣接近的体验，那种感觉与一位热爱正义的

sentences.en: God?
sentences.zh: 上帝亲近的体验？

sentences.en: How do I get more of that experience?
sentences.zh: 我该如何获得更多那样的体验？

sentences.en: And how do I bring about or how do I help in whatever small way I can bring about the world that God would wish to see on earth?
sentences.zh: 我该如何促成，或者我该如何尽我所能，哪怕是一点点，去帮助促成上帝希望在地球上看到的世界？

sentences.en: And how does one get more of the experience of the sacred?
sentences.zh: 那么一个人该如何获得更多神圣的体验呢？

sentences.en: Well, through practice, mostly in my experience.
sentences.zh: 嗯，根据我的经验，主要是通过实践。

sentences.en: I think, you know, that's why people who pray a lot have it more.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，这就是为什么经常祈祷的人会有更多这种体验。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, you know, I was in this deeply impoverished neighborhood in Manila with
sentences.zh: 但同时，我的意思是，你知道，几天前我在马尼拉一个极度贫困的社区，

sentences.en: Doctors Without Borders a couple days ago, watching these profoundly committed healthcare workers try in very difficult circumstances to get people access to good care.
sentences.zh: 和“无国界医生”组织在一起，看着这些深具奉献精神的医护人员在非常困难的情况下，努力让人们获得良好的医疗服务。

sentences.en: And, like, that makes me feel close to God.
sentences.zh: 而且，这让我感觉离上帝很近。

sentences.en: That's a sacred experience for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那是一种神圣的体验。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think kind of in ways both explicit and implicit, we've touched on the idea of hope throughout our conversation.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为在某种程度上，无论是显性的还是隐性的，我们在整个谈话中都触及了希望这个概念。

sentences.en: And are there things that you think adults could learn from teens about hope?
sentences.zh: 你认为成年人能从青少年身上学到关于希望的什么东西吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think we need to put down our armor a little bit, our armor of cynicism and irony and thinking that we know about everything that matters and everything that matters is
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们需要放下一点我们的盔甲，我们那层愤世嫉俗和反讽的盔甲，以及那种认为我们了解所有重要事情，而所有重要的事情就是

sentences.en: how well the minivan handles and how much the mortgage is.
